ops.title: helper install reports success while skipping app redelivery whenever the brew formula is current, leaving a stale deployed bundle and a down helper
ops.description:
`capt-hook helper install` is the documented repair for a broken helper deployment. It currently reports success and exits 0 without repairing anything, whenever the brew formula happens to be current — which is exactly the state a failed post-install leaves behind.

## Observed on yasyf's Mac, 2026-07-25

Starting state after `brew upgrade captain-hook` 12.20.9 -> 12.20.10, whose post-install failed (see cross-reference below):

- brew cellar: **12.20.10**, and `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/captain-hook/12.20.10/libexec/Captain Hook.app/Contents/Info.plist` confirms the payload is 12.20.10
- deployed `~/Applications/Captain Hook.app`: **12.20.9** — `Contents/Helpers/capt-hookd` and `Contents/Info.plist` both unchanged, still dated Jul 25 04:22
- `com.yasyf.capt-hook.helper`: absent from `launchctl list`, GUI helper process not running
- `capt-hook helper status`: `Error: helper not reachable: bridge failed: systemCall(operation: "connect", errno: 61)` (it returned `helper v12.20.9 ok=True` before the upgrade)

Ran the documented repair:

    $ capt-hook helper install
    ...
    Warning: yasyf/tap/captain-hook 12.20.10 is already installed and up-to-date.
    To reinstall 12.20.10, run:
      brew reinstall captain-hook
    Captain Hook installed.

Exit 0, and the final line claims success. Nothing was repaired:

- deployed bundle still **12.20.9**, byte-identical, still dated Jul 25 04:22
- `capt-hook helper status` still `ECONNREFUSED errno 61`
- `com.yasyf.capt-hook.helper` still absent from `launchctl list`

The one side effect it did have was restarting the host daemon (`com.yasyf.captain-hook.host.v1` went from pid 78871 to pid 61736 at 18:10:21) — onto the **same old 12.20.9 image**, since the bundle was never replaced. So the command cycled a live daemon while delivering none of the fix it reported installing.

## Root cause

The success path is gated on **brew formula currency**, not on what is actually deployed. Because the formula was already at 12.20.10, the underlying `brew` call short-circuited with "already installed and up-to-date", the redelivery step never ran, and the wrapper printed its unconditional success line anyway.

Formula currency and deployment currency are different facts. A failed post-install produces precisely the state where they diverge: the formula is current and the deployment is stale. That is the one case `helper install` exists to repair, and it is the one case the current check cannot see.

## Why this is worse than a no-op

The command is what both the brew caveats and the CLI's own help text point users to:

    Captain Hook's signed helper is deployment-owned at:
      ~/Applications/Captain Hook.app
    Repair or reconverge it with:
      capt-hook helper install

A user following that guidance gets `Captain Hook installed.` and reasonably concludes the machine is converged. It is not: the daemon keeps running an old image, and the helper stays down. The silent-success makes a stale deployment indistinguishable from a healthy one — the same class of defect as a health check that cannot fail.

## Suggested fix

1. Gate redelivery on a comparison between the **deployed** bundle's `CFBundleShortVersionString` (and binary identity) and the **cellar payload's**, rather than on brew's formula currency. When they differ, redeliver regardless of what brew reports — `brew reinstall` is available for forcing the payload.
2. Do not print success unconditionally. Report what was actually done: redelivered, or already converged at version X.
3. Treat "skipped redelivery while `helper status` is unreachable" as an error with a non-zero exit and a diagnostic naming the deployed-vs-cellar versions. A repair command that leaves the helper down must not exit 0.
4. Consider whether restarting the host daemon should happen at all on a run that delivered nothing — the restart here was pure cost, disrupting live hook sessions for no change.

## Cross-reference

The upstream trigger was the `brew upgrade captain-hook` post-install failing at the launchd bootstrap step:

    service: install agent "com.yasyf.capt-hook.helper": launchctl bootstrap:
      worker: process exited with code 5: Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error
      (launchd EIO after 6 attempts; desired session "Aqua", current manager "Aqua")

That failure lives in daemonkit's service-install path and is filed separately — see the daemonkit service bootstrap-EIO task. Not duplicated here. This task covers only the captain-hook side: that `helper install`, the designated recovery path from that failure, silently declines to recover.

ops.text: helper install gates redelivery on the DEPLOYED bundle's version vs the cellar payload, not on brew formula currency
A run that skips redelivery while the helper is unreachable exits non-zero with a diagnostic instead of printing success
A stale deployed bundle with a current formula converges to the cellar version in one 'capt-hook helper install' invocation
